messages:
marta: Heads-up — nightly-eval (run id nightly-2026-03-18-03) shows a big regression on the long-context legal-qa prompt set. Failure rate jumped ~2% -> ~22% for sequences >12k. Most failing samples look like the instruction block is being truncated or instruction tokens are dropped mid-stream.

eva: Ugh. Can you paste one of the raw failing generations? Also which model + quantization variant was used in the run?

marta: Model: redwood-ptx-3b-v2 quantized -> q4_0 (autogen). Eval harness used context=32768, stride=16384. Here's a failing sample (copied output):

marta: ```
PROMPT: [INSTRUCTION]
Please extract named parties from the contract below.
... (very long contract, ~14k tokens) ...
GENERATED: 
{"parties": ["ACME LLC", "John Doe"]}
<then suddenly the rest of the instruction disappears and model starts continuing the contract body as if no instruction was present>
```

marta: The marker is clear — around token ~12345 the generation switches context and ignores instruction. Not just formatting.

ajay: That smells like a KV cache offset/wrap bug. I pushed a micro-optim change to kv-offset arithmetic on the q4 codepath last night (commit abcdef1). It used an integer downcast to save memory; could be causing off-by-one at large offsets.

frank: Oncall here — nightly canary included that commit. We should probably roll the canary back if reproduces locally. Can we get a quick local repro?

eva: Trying to reproduce now. Running the eval harness locally with the exact model + quantized artifacts + the same chunking parameters. Command: 

```
python eval/harness.py --run-id reproduce-1782509876 --model redwood-ptx-3b-v2 --quant q4_0 --ctx 32768 --stride 16384 --prompt-file samples/legal-14k.json
```

eva: Quick note: when I run the same prompt on the non-quantized fp16 checkpoint the generation honors the instruction. On q4_0 it drops it consistently at ~12.3k.

liam: Can you share a diff of the logits or the kv-index around the flip point? Even a small offset mismatch could point to pointer arithmetic bug.

marta: Pasted a tiny diff (logits window around the switch):

marta: ```
--- fp16_window.logits  (instruction context preserved)
+++ q4_0_window.logits  (instruction lost)
@@ -3,6 +3,6 @@
 token_12340:  -0.12 vs -0.11
 token_12341:  -0.09 vs -5.34  <-- huge drop in q4 path prob for '::INSTR_END' marker
 token_12342:  -0.08 vs -0.07
```

marta: The INSTR_END token gets an unexpectedly low score on q4 path which makes the model never finish instruction context and keeps consuming contract tokens as continuation.

ajay: That lines up with an index misalignment when reading cached KV pairs; if keys and values are misaligned one token's positional bias could blow up logits for the wrong token. I'll revert abcdef1 from the canary and push a rebuild.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy abcdef1 -> rollback initiated by ajay at 1782510000.

frank: Good. After rollback we should re-run the nightly targeted eval for that prompt set and also run a focused binary search: q4_0 with old kv code vs q4_0 with revert+no other changes.\
liam: Also run a bit-exact test: run a small script that dumps the KV indices + positions at generation step 12330..12350 for both paths. Patch suggestion: add extra asserts in kv reader to check monotonic increasing keys and expected positions.

eva: I added a local instrumented build that logs kv_index entries. Repro script: 

```
python tools/kv_dump.py --model build/q4_0_instrumented --prompt samples/legal-14k.json --steps 12320-12360 > kv_dump_q4.txt
```

eva: Early look shows a single repeated key at pos 12341 on q4 path (duplicate entry), which explains the spike. No duplicates in fp16.

ajay: That duplicate matches the codepath where I attempted to compress empty rows. Looks like compression introduced a stale pointer that sometimes causes duplicate writes at high offsets. I'll open a PR to drop the compression heuristic in q4 until we nail this.

marta: For next steps: 
- ajay revert deployed (done) and canary rolled back (deploy-bot above)
- re-run targeted nightly eval on the legal-14k prompt set (eva)
- add kv_asserts + unit test for duplicate detection (liam/ajay)
- mark affected eval runs in the dashboard and backfill to measure when regression started (marta)

frank: I'll follow up with a postmortem if this regression impacts customer traffic. For now, prioritize fix+tests and a brief note in the incidents channel if we see customer-facing errors.

marta: Thanks all — eva please paste the re-run results when ready. If the re-run shows fail rate back to baseline we can close the triage. :thumbsup:

eva: Re-run done: failure rate dropped back to 1.7% on legal-14k after rollback. Attaching run id nightly-2026-03-18-03-repro.

marta: Closing loop — reproduced, root cause traced to q4 compression micro-opt (duplicate kv write), rollback restored baseline. We'll keep the instrumented tests in CI and gate the compression behind a feature flag.

liam: I'll add the unit test and a short experiment doc describing how to safely re-introduce compression later with fuzzed kv sequences.

marta: Great work.
